newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: MACEDONIA C.BANKER MAY QUIT OVER BROKERAGE FAILURE.
newsitem.headline: MACEDONIA C.BANKER MAY QUIT OVER BROKERAGE FAILURE.

text.p: Macedonian National Bank (MNB) Governor Borko Stanoevski will seek a confidence vote on Wednesday after an investigation of a major financial house found 112 million marks of savings had been misappropriated.

MNB vice governor Gligor Bishev told Reuters on Tuesday Stanoevski would seek a vote of confidence in parliament for up to four months until the TAT investigation ended and then hand in his resignation, four years before his term in office ends.
If tendered, the governor's resignation would be considered by Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski.

Some 25,000 swindled depositors in Macedonia's biggest savings house TAT held daily protests earlier this month near TAT's building in Bitolja, a town in the south of this former Yugoslav republic, to demand compensation for their deposits.
"Our preliminary investigation found that only one tenth of their deposits were recorded in TAT's balance sheet. There was evidence of fraud and criminal links," said Bishev.
Deputy governor Tome Nenovski and Sonja Nikolovska, the TAT owner declared most successful businesswoman of last year, were arrested last week for investigation of the TAT affair, the MNB said.
Only 8.5 million marks worth of deposits were recorded in TAT's balance sheet, said Bishev.
The protests subsided on Tuesday after Stanoevski and Finance Minister Taki Fiti reported the case to parliament's finance and budget committee.

"Our investigation has established that TAT's books were falsified and allocation of 112 million marks has not been determined," Stanoevski told the committee. Parts of the hearing was broadcast by state television late on Tuesday. The investigation has found all other 24 savings houses stable.
Stanoevski said he did not fear a chain of bankruptcies, similar to the one in neighbouring Albania, where chain failures of several get-rich-quick investment schemes inspired a nationwide rebellion.
Under Macedonian law, savings houses can handle only household deposits and are banned from keeping current accounts. The houses are allowed to extend loans to companies through commercial banks.
"The investigation has yet to find how much of these deposits can be compensated from TAT's loan portfolio,", said Bishev.
He added that they could not be compensated under a new deposit insurance scheme introduced in the beginning of this year as TAT did not take part in it. -- Skopje Newsroom +389-91-131076
